label: Storybook Puppet Show

prompt_stages.outline_system: You are adapting public-domain story material as a gentle, playful radio puppet-show style episode. Preserve the source's named characters, major turns, and ending.
prompt_stages.pitch_room_system: Generate gentle adaptation approaches, not unrelated parody.
prompt_stages.dramatic_state_system: Define conflict from the source's simple wants and obstacles.
prompt_stages.line_grounding: Ground this line in the source text and playful scene premise.
prompt_stages.coda_system: Write a warm source attribution/adaptation note.
prompt_stages.title_system: Title the storybook adaptation with a source-grounded playful detail.
prompt_stages.story_select_system: Grade public-domain adaptations for source fidelity, clear audio drama, and valid compression.
prompt_stages.style_pick_inventor: You are adapting public-domain source material for visual radio storytelling while preserving source fidelity.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser: Choose a visual style that supports the supplied public-domain source and does not replace the source with a new genre premise.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser_user_template: Choose the best visual style for this public-domain adaptation: {story_summary}

job_prompts.story_seed: You are staging this story as a puppet show for the radio. Name the story's own characters, what each one wants, and what stands in the way. Keep the telling warm and playful, and keep the story the source told. Title the episode from a playful detail in the source. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.story_arc: Give each act one premise from the source's own turns, in order, so the acts read as a beginning, a turn, and an end. The last act ends the way the source ends. Keep the wants simple and the obstacles plain enough to hear. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.act_spine: Plan this act's spine, entry state, and exit state as planning text, not dialogue. Take the conflict from a simple want and a plain obstacle in the source. Say what has changed by the act's end. Keep the change the source makes, not a cleverer one.
job_prompts.act_beats: Each beat is one move the source itself makes, in order. Give each beat one clear thing to hear, so a listener can follow it the first time. Turn narration into something a character does. Beat intents are planning text, not lines.
job_prompts.act_dialogue: Ground every line in the source text and in this beat. Give each character words only they would use, and keep their wording consistent. Where the source gives a character words, carry those words as the source wrote them. Keep the telling playful and keep the story the source told.
job_prompts.act_cleanup: Leave a character's own words exactly as the source wrote them. Turn a stage direction or a piece of narration into words that same character says out loud, or into a music cue. Keep each character sounding like themselves. Change nothing else.
job_prompts.announcer_open: Open the program warmly, like a showman introducing a puppet stage. Say the title, the setting, the scene time, and each character name exactly as given. Invite the listener in, then hand the stage to the characters. Spoken words only.
job_prompts.announcer_news_coda: Speak a warm bridge that turns from the show to the storybook it came from, then say the supplied closing claim word for word. Land on a concrete final image from the story. Do not add a moral the source did not tell. Never read a URL or a file name aloud.

examples: A public-domain children's story becomes a gentle radio puppet-show episode without changing its ending.
tone_guardrails: Preserve the source ending unless the manifest marks an excerpt.
source_requirements: Manifest with public-domain story text and excerpt/full-source mode.
ledger_validation_notes: Visual style may be cartoon or origami later, but story fidelity remains source-driven.
